   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From John Knight, CHELTENHAM


Dear Ron & Brian,

Thank you for the excellent
service in upgrading my OUTLET
collection to +D disc!

I'd like to keep the originals
safe. Could you let me know how
I can make a back-up copy of my
discs?[+D, Disciple] I tried
SAVE d1 "*" TO d2 but the
destination disc does not save
the whole original.

          Many thanks,

              John

Brian Cavers to John Knight

SAVE d1 "*" to d2 should work OK
and I've just tried it on Issue
47 with no apparent problems. If
you let me know one of the issue
numbers that failed to copy by
this method I will test it on my
set up.Perhaps you have a quirky
drive. Try SAVE d2 "*" to d1 to
see if it makes any difference.

The alternative, since you have
two drives, is to use...

         FORMAT d1 to 2

WARNING! If you don't already
know, the above FORMATS drive 1,
NOT drive 2 then copies drive 2
to 1.Let me know how you get on.
                        - Brian

From Robert Kaminsky, FALMOUTH

There is so much software avail-
able through OUTLET which, if
it were listings in magazines
and books, would be tedious and
time-consuming to enter and then
still need debugging!!

Although I've a copy of MYLGRAPH
(OUTLET 30), I'm still looking
for a sophisticated graph plott-
ing package for the Spectrum. I
have some listings but not the
expertise to get a menu/icon
program together.There does seem
to be a shortage of serious
maths (O level) for the Spectrum
cassette-based 48K. Anyone heard
of CPC MegaMaths? I'm not sure
what that does though!
              - Robert Kaminsky

Brian Cavers to Robert Kaminsky

Maths is not my strong point and
I assume you are talking about
advanced graph plotting such as
sine curves etc. (too advanced
for me!).By comparison,a routine
for menus and icons, in essence,
simply moves a cursor to a
point on the screen which causes
a subroutine to be called. We've
an excellent cursor routine for
the Spectrum in OUTLET 34 called
MULTICURSOR.

If you can describe exactly what
purpose(s) to which you wish to
apply such a program perhaps one
of our readers might know of
some software or even be able to
write a program!
                       - Brian

From: Darell Ottery, SOMERSET

Dear Ron & Brian,

I decided to try to implement a
suggestion I sent to you earlier
about 'Outwrite'. As we have a
huge selection of fonts
available it seemed a good idea
to be able to download the
different fonts to the printer
so a file could be printed in a
different style than the normal
NLQ/draft fonts.

However, I've got problems. One,
the 'Outwrite' fonts are 16 bit
and I'm pretty sure that the
printer (Citizen MSP 20 - Fully
Epson-compatible) only accepts 8
bit fonts.

Can they be converted back using
perhaps a reversal of Charcon?

If not it doesn't really matter
as printout could be done in any
of the hundreds of 8 bit fonts
around. Two, I've managed to
download an 8-bit font O.K. but
when printed it comes out
mirrored and sideways.

I assume that the data needs to
be sent to the printer in a
different manner but I can't
work it out. The only thing I
could come up with was to LOAD
the font into 'Flash' then use
the mirror and rotate functions
to compensate but I haven't
tried that yet.

I am enclosing a copy of my
program both in listing form and
on disc with samples of printout
hoping that you can help me out.


It is designed to use ANY font
taken from the computer rather
than having to design each
character by hand and work out
the data from there. I realise
that by doing this I won't be
able to use proportional spacing
correctly as the width of the
characters is taken as standard
throughout but I thought that
having a multitude of mono-
spaced fonts in a short time was
a lot easier than having to work
hordes of figures out.

I'll also include the relevant
information from the printer
manual in case my printer has
any peculiarities.

        Yours hopefully,

        Darrell Ottery

Brian Cavers to Darrell Ottery

After reading your letter I put
together a quick program that
can load a normal Spectrum or
SAM character set, rotate and/or
mirror each character to create
a new character set and then
save it for future downloading
to a printer. It's in this issue
as FONTWIST. However, I don't
have a printer myself that takes
downloadable fonts so I do not
know if I've overlooked anything
so please let me know if it
needs modifying.

I've done another routine saved
as "FONT16TO8" in ADD-ENDERS to
convert OUTWRITE 16-bit fonts
back to 8-bit.
                        - Brian

   FROM BOB BATES, NOTTINGHAM

I am preparing a review of vari-
ous graphics utilities, clip art
and font sets for the adventure
magazine,"From Beyond",and shall
include mention of your programs
CLIP COMPOSER, RTCLIP,RTCLIP AID
and various pattern generators
that have appeared in the issues
of OUTLET in my possession - the
idea being adventure producers
might use them in preparing
adverts, inlays and storylines
etc. As far as the P.D. clip art
that's been in OUTLET and OUTLET
EXTRA 2 is concerned,I assume it
is legal for it to be included
in PRINTED material which is for
sale but would software houses
be entitled to use it in their
programs?

Also,OUTLET has included various
font sets with the idea that
users should select and use the
fonts in their own programs,e.g.
TRILOGY (OUTLET 37). Would it be
permissible for programmers and
software houses to include
these sets in programs which are
for sale?

Would it be possible for them to
use fonts in PRINTED material
included with their adventures?

Sorry to trouble you with these
questions but the whole area is
rather confused.

        Yours sincerely,

            Bob Bates

Brian Cavers to Bob Bates

You can definitely use character
sets and clip art in printed
material. You can use any fonts
from in OUTLET in programs for
sale unless the author states
you cannot.I cannot think of any
in this category. THE COLLECTION
in Issue 14 tells you how to put
them in "Quilled" adventures.

The use of public domain clip
art in programs for sale is, I
believe, also acceptable. I know
of no precedant to the contrary
and can see no harm in it but it
is hard to be 100% positive. I
doubt anyone would object but
you may prefer to advise against
such use.              - Brian

From: Norman Unitt,
      STRATFORD-on-AVON

Dear Ron and Brian,

Thank you for your reply to my
query in Outlet 46 asking about
Masterfile. Unhappily Microsnips
are no longer able to supply.

On to Peter Wheeler's letter in
Outlet 48. For some time I had
been unhappy about the content
of Outlet since the arrival of
Sam. I prepared a letter to you
some months ago to complain of
the lot of the Microdrive
subscribers. There seemed to be
less and less for us and then to
add insult to injury came the
Addenders. Here we were paying

the highest subscription and
getting less than the disc
people!


I had suggested in my unposted
letter that the Sam stuff should
all go in Addenders. My letter
did not get sent as I thought it
too cruel. I considered several
options - first to give up
Outlet, this I could not do as I
have had such pleasure since the
very first issue, second to buy
a Sam. This also was rejected as
I could not see myself changing
my complete set-up at my time of
life! Thirdly to buy a disc-
drive. This, I am happy to say,
has proved a great success.

In my opinion, Sam does seem to
be getting over exposure but
then we must move with the times
and you are running a business
although it always seems like a
very nice club. Rest assured I
shall renew my subscription.

Format,the disc magazine,is also
going over to Sam I find. That
subscription will go I fear.

Does anyone know if TASWORD 3
can be converted for use on
disc?

             Regards

          Norman Unitt

Brian Cavers to Norman Unitt

Thanks for your comments,Norman.
I'm sure you appreciate that its
the high cost of the microdrive
cartridges and the low capacity
that makes them unfair! One 3.5"
OUTLET disc can hold 780K and
costs less than 50p. The same
OUTLET needs TWO microdrive
cartridges (currently costing
about SIX POUNDS for two blank
cartridges from probably the
only remaining supplier: EEC).We
are using up our dwindling stock
which we obtained for under `2 a
cartridge - but still a cost to
us of the best part of `4 for
the two OUTLET cartridges!Yet we
still sell it for less than EEC
does for blanks!!!!

As for the proportion of SAM to
Spectrum material in OUTLET it's
worth repeating that OUTLET is
bigger anyway with ADD-ENDERS
but most importantly,we can only
publish what we receive. By the
way, I do strive to keep stuff
of general interest in the main
OUTLET and SAM or +3 or Disciple
specific material in ADD-ENDERS.
Again, I think it's well worth
repeating, WE HAVE NO POLICY OF
PROPORTION OF SAM TO SPECTRUM
WHATSOEVER -WE JUST PUBLISH WHAT
IS RECEIVED. I am considering
things like a separate editorial
and LOOKOUT etc. Really this may
just mean that the SAM info will
be cut from the Spectrum version
and vice-versa but I'll keep on
thinking about this and welcome
others' ideas.

TRANSFORM, 7c Station Approach,
Hayes, Kent, BR2 7EQ (Tel: 081
462 4666) may do MASTERFILE.I've
an old advert with it listed at
`14.95.I'm sure this is the tape
version but it's easily altered
to any drive syntax. It will be
ZX printer only. They also list
MF-PRINT at `6.95 which enables
you to use a full-size printer
or both MASTERFILE and MF-PRINT
together at `19.95. In addition,
they had MASTERFILE + MF-PRINT
on Disciple or Opus Discovery
disc at `22.95. This may be the
one to go for but you must tell
them your system! If you write,
ask them if they still supply
Disciple interfaces just out of
interest!
                        - Brian

From Carlo M. Vireca, ITALY


Using OMNIVAC from OUTLET 28 by
Ian Wooff I found a little bug.
I think OMNIVAC is a very useful
program that I'm often compelled
to use to compress large BASIC
programs. What is the bug?


OMNIVAC is embroiled by DEF FN,
e.g., DEF FN a(b)=... is changed
to:   DEF FN a(bVAL"")=...

VAL""has no meaning and produces
a parameter error when called.It
is a small bug and easily edited
and DEF FN is normally seldom
used but I thought it adviseable
that readers know of it.

In reply to Ken Stearn in OUTLET
45 I read the request to alter
HARD 24 to get full-size pages.
I, myself, am working to improve
HARD 24 for dumps in different
sizes.

The principal aim I gave myself,
in reality, was to obtain a dump
like a stamp (little).I tried to
print full pages but the print
head,for solid backgrounds, gets
red-hot.I fear it's not suitable
for a long life!

At present I'm working to debug
some routines,full-page too, and
after summer I hope to reach an
OUTLET version (but the biggest
task is the English writing!).

Many thanks, Carlo.      - Brian

Brian Cavers to Kevin Cooper

Regarding our compressed text, I
finally managed to get my method
of converting it back to Tasword
2 format to work using MASTERDOS
and you will probably have seen
my program "OPENOUTLET" in last
month's issue.

The actual method of compression
we devised replaces lower case
vowels and the next character
with a single character using
the fact that many of the 256
possible characters are unused
in normal text, e.g. the "ex" of
text might become say, character
205. All spaces at the end of
lines are replaced by character
13.

Yes, I'm sure we've considered
marking envelopes "MAGNETIC
MATERIAL" but we have no hard
evidence that (a)the Post Office
xray equipment can corrupt a
magnetic disc, (b) if it could,
that it happens often enough to
worry about (c)even if we marked
envelopes the Post Office would
take any notice. If you receive
a corrupt disc it may be due to
a number of things. How can you
tell?

Yes,the SAM's going off-tune may
be a faulty crystal or it may
just need re-adjusting in the
PSU unit. It's probably best to
consult PBT if you are unsure as
I think there are a few high
voltages in the PSU.

I can't find the Tasword 2's key
pokes either. It must be in the
OUTLETTERS pages between Issues
32 to 38 is my guess! You might
try POKE 23561,10 : POKE 23562,3
in the Tas BASIC itself. If they
work then adjust the values 10
and 3 to suit your taste.

Regarding my editing letters I
try not to change personal
expressions like "Speccy" but I
correct spelling and grammar as
best I can - just as any news-
paper or magazine does. It's
nothing to do with any area of
the country but simply improved
communication and understanding
with the greatest number of
people using a common language.
                        - Brian

From: Malcolm Perry,
      KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Ron and Brian,

I do not know if this has been
mentioned before as I am not up
to date with SAM articles in
OUTLET. I wanted to make up a
disc that would BOOT and
AUTOload both Disciple and Sam.
Quickly passing by the obvious
question "why would anyone in
their right mind want to put
both Spectrum and Sam files on
the same disc?" we will proceed!

There is no problem in putting
the different BOOT DOS files as
each looks for a different
thing.

The problem came with the
AUTOLOAD file. Neither system
will LOAD the other directly.

A solution is to alter the SAM
DOS so it looks for a different
file name. The file name "AUTO*"
is held in DVAR 7572 (to 7581)
so a new name can be POKEd in
and revised DOS SAVEd. The error
report"no auto file"has the auto
starting at DVAR 3989 so can be
changed if required(Masterdos is
8634 and 3931 respectively).

The"new name" AUTOLOAD file can,
when LOADed, POKE the AUTO back
to restore normal operation. An
alternative use is to make the
F9 key look for a file other
than "AUTO" once booted.

Out of interest: in the Disciple
running GDOS,the name is at 1339
and running UNIDOS at 505.
(UNIDOS is POKE @ 505 but GDOS
needs the offset to be consider-
ed i.e., 1339-664). The +D seems
to have the name in ROM so
cannot be changed in that case.

Here are a few comments relating
to points raised in OUTLET 48.

The +D problem raised by Chris
Ingram. Some while back I had
problems of used and current
sectors being overwritten with
new data hence corrupting other
files. I suspected at the time
it was due to a dirty edge
connector and I still believe it
played a part.

It was noticed that,on Disciple,
corrupted discs occured prior to
noticeable problems of crashing
due to the edge connector. I
suspect data line contacts were
causing problems but not suffic-
iently then to actually cause a
crash. With a Disciple,the worst
time is the first 5 minutes or
so of switch-on as things are
warming up and expanding causing
movement of the interface in
respect to the Spectrum.

After cleaning the connector and
further periodic cleaning,so far
the problem has not repeated. I
have also had two causes of
corrupted discs. First was my
fault! I started a SAVE and got
an"overwrite"message so thought:
"wrong disc!".

I changed the disc and pressed a
key to do the SAVE. At that
moment the disc map [in RAM] was
for the old disc so pressing "y"
wrote to sectors that related to
the old disc - NOT the new - so
used sectors could obviously be
overwritten.The error of my ways
eventually dawned on me that you
can't do that! You must say "no"
and start the SAVE again.

The other time was when a disc
became corrupted and I found a
program file had actually been
SAVEd into the directory tracks
which in theory should be
impossible.This was tracked down
when I realised it only happened
after a number of programs were
on the disc and it was starting
to use side 2.

The ribbon cable was faulty
where it went into the connector
and the "side select" signal was
not getting to the drive every
time so while the Disciple was
sending "select side 2" the
drive was staying on side 1 and
so writing to directory tracks.
After remaking the connector the
fault has not reappeared so I am
certain that was the problem.


Regarding 'OUTWRITE!' and your
comment about the comms inter-
face missing the first byte
sent,I use the printer interface
from Format and if I understand
the problem you described, the
following would fail (cause the
printer to BEEP: CHR$ 7).

Switch Sam on from cold. Enter
as a direct command CLOSE #3 :
OPEN #3;"B" : LPRINT CHR$ 7. I
can confirm it worked O.K. so
does that answer the query about
"other printer interfaces"?

Now a question to you. After a
printout you are asked if you
want a repeat. A "no" causes the
printer to do a LF and then you
return to text edit. If you say
"Y" then printing starts without
doing a LF first so line 1 over-
writes the last line printed.
There are obviously ways to
prevent this now, I know, but I
wondered if I had missed some-
thing obvious in setting it up.
I think I have gone through all
the variations possible in
setting up my printer.

My set up requires a LF to be
sent to the printer which does
not do auto LF on CR.

SAM disc problems: You mentioned
problems of having some discs
returned and a suspect drive. I
will mention the following of
interest but at the moment I do
not know the full implications.
Out of some 40 discs,5 failed to
format. On SAM,one was a branded
TDK the remaining were cheap
unbranded.

Out of interest I tried them on
the +D and they all formatted.It
proved that they totally failed
to format on Sam D1 but were
100% O.K. on Sam D2 and 4 drives
on Disciple and +D.

I decided d1 on Sam was to blame
but swapping over drives in Sam
it was still D1 that failed to
format so it almost looks like
something in Sam itself that is
more fussy on discs. It is also
interesting that the "failed"
disc, when formatted on another
drive, is then read O.K. by the
drive that failed to format it.
I also proved the format failure
is in the original laying down
of tracks and sectors. Now I am
wondering what the implications
are of a disc that had been
formatted on d2 but would have
failed on d1 if subsequently
used to SAVE data in d1 while it
finds the sectors etc., O.K. Is
the data going to be written to
the disc reliably or not?

Until this came to light, discs
were formatted haphazardly on
any system and used with any
other - it does make you think.

There is also the fact that head
alignment can be out a bit and
while say, 90% cope, there is
the possibility of one being out
in the opposite direction to
another - sufficiently to cause
problems even though they seem
O.K. with other drives.

          Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

Thanks Malcolm. Regarding why
anyone would want to put both
SAM and Spectrum files on the
same disc - I myself do! All the
files contributed to OUTLET are
obviously transferred to my
discs and the user's media is
returned. At one time I had sets
of microdrive cartridges, +3
discs, Opus and eventually on
SAM and Disciple too! It made it
difficult to look through my
records so now everything goes
on a single series of discs that
can be used by SAM or Spectrum.
The first file in the directory
is the SAM dos file.Next is the
SAM CATLOADER then the Disciple
CATLOADER.

To load a SAM file I can just
press F9 and press a key when it
is displayed by CATLOADER. It
does not matter if I have reset
the SAM or not as the dos is
booted in automatically if not
present.


To load a Spectrum file I type:
LOAD P3 which loads the Spectrum
CATLOADER and, again, a single
keypress will load the program.
One of the strengths of the +D
and Disciple is that,unlike SAM,
if you do a reset the dos is not
lost so one rarely needs to re-
boot the dos and even if it were
on the disc I would normally be
typing LOAD P1 or LOAD P2 to
boot CATLOADER anyway!

I thought about your idea of
changing the name of the boot
file on SAM but then I would be
unable to boot other people's
AUTO file - or even the OUTLET
AUTO loader.

The disc corruption problems are
all very worrying and I despair
of achieving reliability.

Your printer test does indeed
suggest that the"first-byte-lost
-after-switch-on" bug is in the
comms interface - not in the SAM
itself but it's not conclusive.
For one thing, I have found some
bugs only happen in a running
program -not in a direct command
and also, perhaps the byte is
only lost if part of a string of
codes sent to the printer.

I've just done a test myself but
I can't get the bug to occur!!!
I tried...

10 OPEN #3;"B"
20 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"@"

This clears the printer of all
codes and on my BROTHER M1009 (I
don't know whether others do it)
the print head jerks back to the
left with a loud double-click.

In my test,I expected it to miss
the CHR$ 27 and just print the
"@" because I've not yet used
the SAM this morning. I have had
this happen many, many times
before. However, it cleared the
printer correctly in this test!
Clearly, there is more to this
bug than we know!

Regarding the "repeat copy"
problem in OUTWRITE this came
about because the author, Bob
Wilkinson, only uses cut-sheet
paper so he always manually puts
in a new sheet at that point
whereas I only use tractor feed
and need to return to do a form
feed anyway so neither of us
really spotted this hiccup! You
use roll paper which means you
must wind the paper on.This will
be looked at in the future
upgrade version of OUTWRITE.

                       - Brian.

From: Malcolm Perry, KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Ron and Brian,

I do not know if this has been mentioned before as I am not up to date with SAM articles in OUTLET. I wanted to make up a disc that would BOOT and AUTOload both Disciple and Sam. Quickly passing by the obvious question "why would anyone in their right mind want to put both Spectrum and Sam files on the same disc?" we will proceed!

There is no problem in putting the different BOOT DOS files as each looks for a different thing.

The problem came with the AUTOLOAD file. Neither system will LOAD the other directly.

A solution is to alter the SAM DOS so it looks for a different file name. The file name "AUTO*" is held in DVAR 7572 (to 7581) so a new name can be POKEd in and revised DOS SAVEd. The error report"no auto file"has the auto starting at DVAR 3989 so can be changed if required(Masterdos is 8634 and 3931 respectively).

The"new name" AUTOLOAD file can, when LOADed, POKE the AUTO back to restore normal operation. An alternative use is to make the F9 key look for a file other than "AUTO" once booted.

Out of interest: in the Disciple running GDOS,the name is at 1339 and running UNIDOS at 505. (UNIDOS is POKE @ 505 but GDOS needs the offset to be consider- ed i.e., 1339-664). The +D seems to have the name in ROM so cannot be changed in that case.

Here are a few comments relating to points raised in OUTLET 48.

The +D problem raised by Chris Ingram. Some while back I had problems of used and current sectors being overwritten with new data hence corrupting other files. I suspected at the time it was due to a dirty edge connector and I still believe it played a part.

It was noticed that,on Disciple, corrupted discs occured prior to noticeable problems of crashing due to the edge connector. I suspect data line contacts were causing problems but not suffic- iently then to actually cause a crash. With a Disciple,the worst time is the first 5 minutes or so of switch-on as things are warming up and expanding causing movement of the interface in respect to the Spectrum.

After cleaning the connector and further periodic cleaning,so far the problem has not repeated. I have also had two causes of corrupted discs. First was my fault! I started a SAVE and got an"overwrite"message so thought: "wrong disc!".

I changed the disc and pressed a key to do the SAVE. At that moment the disc map [in RAM] was for the old disc so pressing "y" wrote to sectors that related to the old disc - NOT the new - so used sectors could obviously be overwritten.The error of my ways eventually dawned on me that you can't do that! You must say "no" and start the SAVE again.

The other time was when a disc became corrupted and I found a program file had actually been SAVEd into the directory tracks which in theory should be impossible.This was tracked down when I realised it only happened after a number of programs were on the disc and it was starting to use side 2.

The ribbon cable was faulty where it went into the connector and the "side select" signal was not getting to the drive every time so while the Disciple was sending "select side 2" the drive was staying on side 1 and so writing to directory tracks. After remaking the connector the fault has not reappeared so I am certain that was the problem.

Regarding 'OUTWRITE!' and your comment about the comms inter- face missing the first byte sent,I use the printer interface from Format and if I understand the problem you described, the following would fail (cause the printer to BEEP: CHR$ 7).

Switch Sam on from cold. Enter as a direct command CLOSE #3 : OPEN #3;"B" : LPRINT CHR$ 7. I can confirm it worked O.K. so does that answer the query about "other printer interfaces"?

Now a question to you. After a printout you are asked if you want a repeat. A "no" causes the printer to do a LF and then you return to text edit. If you say "Y" then printing starts without doing a LF first so line 1 over- writes the last line printed. There are obviously ways to prevent this now, I know, but I wondered if I had missed some- thing obvious in setting it up. I think I have gone through all the variations possible in setting up my printer.

My set up requires a LF to be sent to the printer which does not do auto LF on CR.

SAM disc problems: You mentioned problems of having some discs returned and a suspect drive. I will mention the following of interest but at the moment I do not know the full implications. Out of some 40 discs,5 failed to format. On SAM,one was a branded TDK the remaining were cheap unbranded.

Out of interest I tried them on the +D and they all formatted.It proved that they totally failed to format on Sam D1 but were 100% O.K. on Sam D2 and 4 drives on Disciple and +D.

I decided d1 on Sam was to blame but swapping over drives in Sam it was still D1 that failed to format so it almost looks like something in Sam itself that is more fussy on discs. It is also interesting that the "failed" disc, when formatted on another drive, is then read O.K. by the drive that failed to format it. I also proved the format failure is in the original laying down of tracks and sectors. Now I am wondering what the implications are of a disc that had been formatted on d2 but would have failed on d1 if subsequently used to SAVE data in d1 while it finds the sectors etc., O.K. Is the data going to be written to the disc reliably or not?

Until this came to light, discs were formatted haphazardly on any system and used with any other - it does make you think.

There is also the fact that head alignment can be out a bit and while say, 90% cope, there is the possibility of one being out in the opposite direction to another - sufficiently to cause problems even though they seem O.K. with other drives.

Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry

Thanks Malcolm. Regarding why anyone would want to put both SAM and Spectrum files on the same disc - I myself do! All the files contributed to OUTLET are obviously transferred to my discs and the user's media is returned. At one time I had sets of microdrive cartridges, +3 discs, Opus and eventually on SAM and Disciple too! It made it difficult to look through my records so now everything goes on a single series of discs that can be used by SAM or Spectrum. The first file in the directory is the SAM dos file.Next is the SAM CATLOADER then the Disciple CATLOADER.

To load a SAM file I can just press F9 and press a key when it is displayed by CATLOADER. It does not matter if I have reset the SAM or not as the dos is booted in automatically if not present.

To load a Spectrum file I type: LOAD P3 which loads the Spectrum CATLOADER and, again, a single keypress will load the program. One of the strengths of the +D and Disciple is that,unlike SAM, if you do a reset the dos is not lost so one rarely needs to re- boot the dos and even if it were on the disc I would normally be typing LOAD P1 or LOAD P2 to boot CATLOADER anyway!

I thought about your idea of changing the name of the boot file on SAM but then I would be unable to boot other people's AUTO file - or even the OUTLET AUTO loader.

The disc corruption problems are all very worrying and I despair of achieving reliability.

Your printer test does indeed suggest that the"first-byte-lost -after-switch-on" bug is in the comms interface - not in the SAM itself but it's not conclusive. For one thing, I have found some bugs only happen in a running program -not in a direct command and also, perhaps the byte is only lost if part of a string of codes sent to the printer.

I've just done a test myself but I can't get the bug to occur!!! I tried...

10 OPEN #3;"B" 20 LPRINT CHR$ 27;"@"

This clears the printer of all codes and on my BROTHER M1009 (I don't know whether others do it) the print head jerks back to the left with a loud double-click.

In my test,I expected it to miss the CHR$ 27 and just print the "@" because I've not yet used the SAM this morning. I have had this happen many, many times before. However, it cleared the printer correctly in this test! Clearly, there is more to this bug than we know!
